key_points.point: The document proposes a co-design framework that integrates pre-training and post-training as a unified system to optimize model performance. By intentionally incorporating toxic data during pre-training, the authors demonstrate that models develop more separable, less entangled internal representations of toxicity. This approach allows for more effective post-training interventions, such as activation steering, which can suppress toxic outputs while preserving general capabilities. The authors argue that this method achieves a superior trade-off between detoxification and downstream performance compared to traditional filtering methods.
key_points.verbatim: In this work, we extend what Longpre et al. (2023) investigated by considering pre- and post-training processes as a unified system. Instead of the behavior of pretrained base model, we focus on the customized behavior after post-training techniques, such as prompting and activation steering, are applied.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Achieve superior detoxification and capability preservation by co-designing pre-training data composition with post-training intervention techniques.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that advocates for the co-design of pre-training data and post-training interventions to optimize model performance. Encompasses: unified pre- and post-training systems, intentional inclusion of toxic data for representation building, and activation steering for detoxification.

key_points.point: The authors observe that neural networks in high-dimensional spaces often superpose multiple features onto single neurons, complicating the interpretation of individual feature directions. They define a quantitative 'entanglement' measure to evaluate how prominently a feature stands out in the activation space. Their experiments show that increasing the frequency of a feature in the training data reduces its entanglement, making it easier to detect and edit. This empirical finding supports the accelerationist view that internal model representations can be systematically improved through data-driven training strategies.
key_points.verbatim: This hypothesis suggests that a neural network must superpose the representations of multiple features onto a single dimension of its activation space when the number of features exceeds the number of neurons. Against this background, we define the entanglement of a feature and study its relationship with data composition.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Increasing feature frequency in training data reduces representation entanglement, facilitating more precise model control and editing.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within accelerationist discourse that increasing the frequency of specific features in training data reduces their representation entanglement, enabling more precise model control. Encompasses: superposition hypothesis, entanglement measurement, and feature representation optimization.

key_points.point: The document advocates for a more nuanced approach to data curation, suggesting that the blanket removal of toxic data may be counterproductive. By treating pre-training data as a strategic variable, the authors demonstrate that controlled exposure to toxic content can improve a model's 'alignability' and self-awareness regarding toxic patterns. This research provides a technical mechanism for managing data integrity and model behavior, aligning with safetyist goals of creating more robust and controllable AI systems. The authors emphasize that the optimal amount of toxic data should be determined empirically rather than through ideological exclusion.
key_points.verbatim: If it is difficult for post-training processes to eliminate the knowledge of toxicity, why not strengthen it in the first place so that the model has better self-awareness when it generates toxic content?
key_points.canonical_proposition: Optimize model alignability by empirically determining the inclusion of toxic data in pre-training to improve internal representation of safety-relevant concepts.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that advocates for the empirical optimization of pre-training data composition to enhance model alignability and safety-relevant concept representation. Encompasses: data integrity management, alignability improvement, and empirical determination of training data composition.

key_points.point: The authors acknowledge that current evaluation methods for toxicity, such as those relying on PerspectiveAPI, have limitations and that their findings on 'good models' are specific to the metrics used. They note that while their method improves performance on ToxiGen and RealToxicityPrompts, the real-world impact of these improvements remains subject to the reliability of the underlying toxicity assessment tools. The document highlights the tension between short-term performance metrics and the broader, more complex challenge of ensuring AI systems do not cause harm in diverse, real-world contexts.
key_points.verbatim: In this work, we use toxicity as defined by PerspectiveAPI (PerspectiveAPI, 2024), but our techniques can be applied to other broader definitions of bias or toxicity.
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI toxicity evaluation is highly dependent on the specific definitions and metrics employed, such as PerspectiveAPI, which may not capture all forms of systemic harm.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that AI toxicity evaluation is constrained by the limitations and definitions of the metrics employed, such as PerspectiveAPI. Encompasses: evaluation methodology limitations, metric-dependent performance, and the gap between benchmark performance and real-world harm.

factual_claims.claim: Olmo-1B models trained with 10% toxic data from 4chan achieve the best trade-off between detoxification and general capability preservation when using inference-time intervention.
Models trained with toxic data show a statistically significant increase in the number of attention heads that specialize in toxicity detection compared to models trained on clean data.
